value.rationale: Interaction truncation is a natural operation in ANOVA and approximation of multivariate functions. The result determines worst-case maximum-norm stability for every full-support finite product law and every cutoff, gives extremizing sign inputs, identifies uniform marginals as universal minimizers, and computes an all-order sharp stability envelope with order-of-growth and a nonmonotonic nested-range example. These structural results go beyond low-degree examples or routine relabeling, although no general correlated-measure claim is made.
